{"caption":"Video and photos by @babaktafreshi | On Tuesday morning I photographed a celestial spectacle right in my backyard, near Boston. Hidden behind the moon for an hour, Jupiter reappeared from the dark night side of the moon, like a sparkling diamond. The rare phenomenon is called occultation. 

Slide 1: timelapse videos of the scene through a 600mm telephoto lens (cropped). Note the four lined up Galilean Moons of Jupiter. 
Slide 2: Moon is departing away from the alignment in twilight. 
Slide 3: An HDR image (3 exposures) to reveal the lunar details in both its bright dayside and the faint earthshine glow on the night side of the moon. 
Slide 4: A longer 30-second exposure on a star tracker has overexposed the moon to reveal the background starry sky.","likes":180004,"comments":410,"photoCount":3,"videoCoverCount":1}

{"caption":"Presented by @rolex. Veterinarian and Rolex National Geographic Perpetual Planet Explorer Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka is helping to protect these endangered primates through her pioneering One Health approach, which starts with treating the gorillas’ closest neighbors—focusing on diseases that can be transmitted between humans and animals.

{"caption":"Presented by @Rolex. Conservation ecologist and Rolex National Geographic Perpetual Planet Explorer Matt Shirley has spent years working alongside scientists across Africa to uncover the secret lives of dwarf crocodiles, a timid species that emerges from burrows at night to feed. Despite thriving in a variety of ecosystems, the world’s smallest crocodiles are facing commercial overharvesting and habitat loss. Through his work, Shirley is discovering the ways these tenacious reptiles are hanging on and adapting to their ever-changing environment.

caption.text:
Presented by @Rolex. Welcome to Africa 🌍 Africa Earth’s Wild Home takes you deep into the heart of our wildest continent, bringing you closer to its animals, landscapes, and the people watching over it than ever before.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

Africa Earth’s Wild Home, narrated by @wunmimosaku, premieres Friday, October 2 at 8/7c on National Geographic. Streaming next day on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

caption.text:
Video and photos by @babaktafreshi | On Tuesday morning I photographed a celestial spectacle right in my backyard, near Boston. Hidden behind the moon for an hour, Jupiter reappeared from the dark night side of the moon, like a sparkling diamond. The rare phenomenon is called occultation. 

Slide 1: timelapse videos of the scene through a 600mm telephoto lens (cropped). Note the four lined up Galilean Moons of Jupiter. 
Slide 2: Moon is departing away from the alignment in twilight. 
Slide 3: An HDR image (3 exposures) to reveal the lunar details in both its bright dayside and the faint earthshine glow on the night side of the moon. 
Slide 4: A longer 30-second exposure on a star tracker has overexposed the moon to reveal the background starry sky.

We could stay here a while. 🌿

#Queens is streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

caption.text:
Presented by @Rolex. Fertile for just one week per year, this female fossa can't afford to be shy. 

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

#AfricaEarthsWildHome is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

caption.text:
Many orphaned giant anteater pups in Brazil are still nursing when their mothers are killed in road collisions. At rehabilitation centers, caregivers bottle-feed them, provide around-the-clock care, and help them build strength for a possible return to the wild. Nat Geo Explorer @fernando.faciole spent three years documenting these young animals and the people caring for them.

See how researchers are making Brazil's roads safer for giant anteaters at the link in bio.

caption.text:
In the Alaska Peninsula, a brown bear surrounds a school of sockeye salmon that had journeyed thousands of miles upstream to the freshwaters of Alaska from the Pacific Ocean. Photographer @mikerigney told National Geographic this salmon migration was "easily one of the most beautiful natural displays I've ever seen."

See more Photos of the Day at the link in bio.

Alzheimer’s disease symptoms and other forms of dementia don't occur overnight. Up to a decade before memory impairment appears, subtle cognitive symptoms can emerge. While these signs alone aren't definitive, recognizing patterns can help patients and families prepare for what lies ahead.

Learn more about these signs and what experts say patients and their families can do at the link in bio.

Photograph by Jason Edwards (@jasonedwardsng)

Presented by @Rolex. Hunted for their scales and meat, pangolins are among the most heavily trafficked mammals in the world, with millions believed to have been harvested in Africa over recent decades. But in places like Cameroon, conservationists are working to protect these armored creatures. At the @tikkihywoodfoundation's rescue center, staff and minders tend to injured pangolins before rehabilitating them for release into the wild, managing complex care needs that can change from day to day. 

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in #AfricaEarthsWildHome. #PerpetualPlanet

Learn more about the efforts to save pangolins at the link in bio. 

Photographs by @marcuswestbergphotography

caption.text: The shoebill’s prehistoric appearance makes it unique among living birds, with a look that matches fossils dating back millions of years. Its biology gets stranger still, with chicks attacking their own siblings and adults hunting everything from lungfish to baby crocodiles. Learn more about shoebills with these five facts.

caption.text:
Presented by @Rolex. Madagascar is currently home to over one hundred species of lemurs that aren't found anywhere else on the planet, and scientists have uncovered evidence of even more lemur species that roamed Madagascar in the past, including giants that were far larger than any of today's lemurs.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

#AfricaEarthsWildHome is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

Presented by @rolex. Around 40,000 tourists visit Bwindi Impenetrable National Park annually, bringing pathogens from around the world that can put the mountain gorillas who live there at risk. Veterinarian and Rolex National Geographic Perpetual Planet Explorer Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka is helping to protect these endangered primates through her pioneering One Health approach, which starts with treating the gorillas’ closest neighbors—focusing on diseases that can be transmitted between humans and animals.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in #AfricaEarthsWildHome. #PerpetualPlanet

Learn more about Kalema-Zikusoka pioneering work and this difficult-to-implement approach to wildlife conservation in the October issue of National Geographic and at the link in bio. 

Photograph by Robin Hammond (@hammond_robin)

Photos by @joelsartore | Isn’t Dumpling just the cutest?

With short, stubby legs, it isn’t easy for striped skunks to outrun trouble, so they’ve developed a unique defense system to protect themselves from predators. When cornered, a skunk will first try to frighten the predator by turning its back, raising its tail, and arching its back while stomping its feet. If this display proves unsuccessful, the skunk will resort to spraying the animal with a strong-smelling fluid that can sting the eyes of the predator, giving the skunk just enough time to escape.

Photos taken @savannah_wrc_. To see more species featured in the Photo Ark, follow me @joelsartore. #PhotoArk

This king penguin parent and its chick were among thousands that caught the eye of photographer Martin Gregus Jr. (@mywildlive) on South Georgia. King penguins have an unusually long reproductive cycle compared to other penguins, which means that eggs, chicks, and adults can all be present within a colony at the same time.

Presented by @Rolex. Meet the dwarf crocodiles thriving in the darkness of Gabon’s caves. From hunting bats to navigating cave floors coated in guano, these remarkable reptiles have found unexpected ways to survive. Learn more about Africa's tiny crocs and Matt Shirley's research at the link in bio.

Photographs by @hammond_robin
 
#AfricaEarthsWildHome is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

Women in this Sardinian mountain village have high odds of living to 100. Researchers have identified it as a new blue zone—a geographic region where residents aged 70 and older have exceptional rates of survival and longevity. Here, women who reach 70 are three times as likely to reach the century mark as their U.S. counterparts, so researchers are investigating whether factors such as diet, family life, and genetics could help explain that advantage.

Discover the clues to living a longer, healthier life at the link in bio.

Photograph by Marisa Montibeller

Presented by @Rolex. Would you ever have guessed that flamingos are growing their own food with the help of fiddler crabs? This arrangement is so unusual, it's never been seen anywhere else on Earth.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

See more extraordinary animal behavior in #AfricaEarthsWildHome, now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

caption.text:
A simple branch becomes a fishing rod in the hands of these resourceful chimpanzees. This technique allows them to harvest algae without getting wet.
 
Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet
 
Presented by @Rolex. #AfricaEarthsWildHome is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

caption.text:
Presented by @Rolex. Conservation ecologist and Rolex National Geographic Perpetual Planet Explorer Matt Shirley has spent years working alongside scientists across Africa to uncover the secret lives of dwarf crocodiles, a timid species that emerges from burrows at night to feed. Despite thriving in a variety of ecosystems, the world’s smallest crocodiles are facing commercial overharvesting and habitat loss. Through his work, Shirley is discovering the ways these tenacious reptiles are hanging on and adapting to their ever-changing environment. 

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in #AfricaEarthsWildHome. #PerpetualPlanet

Discover more about dwarf crocodiles and the conservation plans to help them thrive at the link in bio.

Photograph by Robin Hammond (@hammond_robin)

Presented by @Rolex. When the millionaire who owned the world's largest rhino herd ran out of money, the conservationists who took over responsibility for the herd in 2023 had an audacious idea: split 2,000 southern white rhinos into smaller groups and seed them across Africa. The goal is to protect them from poachers and ensure the species has the best chance of survival. While the plan is working, their mission is far from over. 

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in #AfricaEarthsWildHome. #PerpetualPlanet

Learn more about this historic plan to save the white rhino at the link in bio.

Photographs by @brentstirton

Presented by @Rolex. He’s spent six months underground, and now he’s looking for love—but when a female answers his call, this black frog seems to have second thoughts.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

#AfricaEarthsWildHome is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

Presented by @Rolex. It's time to explore nature on an epic scale. It's time to explore Africa. 

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

#AfricaEarthsWildHome is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

caption.text:
Presented by @Rolex. When Matt Shirley first shone his flashlight into a cave in Gabon, dozens of crocodile eyes stared back at him. But these weren’t ordinary crocodiles. They were tiny, timid, and...orange. They had found an unlikely home underground, and an unusual source of food that helped them thrive. Discover more about the lives of Africa’s smallest crocodiles at the link in bio.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in #AfricaEarthsWildHome. #PerpetualPlanet

Photograph by @hammond_robin

Africa Earth’s Wild Home premieres Friday, October 2 at 8/7c on @NatGeoTV. Streaming next day on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

Video and photos by @babaktafreshi | On Tuesday morning I photographed a celestial spectacle right in my backyard, near Boston. Hidden behind the moon for an hour, Jupiter reappeared from the dark night side of the moon, like a sparkling diamond. The rare phenomenon is called occultation. 

Slide 1: timelapse videos of the scene through a 600mm telephoto lens (cropped). Note the four lined up Galilean Moons of Jupiter. 
Slide 2: Moon is departing away from the alignment in twilight. 
Slide 3: An HDR image (3 exposures) to reveal the lunar details in both its bright dayside and the faint earthshine glow on the night side of the moon. 
Slide 4: A longer 30-second exposure on a star tracker has overexposed the moon to reveal the background starry sky.

posts.caption:
Presented by @Rolex. Fertile for just one week per year, this female fossa can't afford to be shy. 

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

#AfricaEarthsWildHome is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

posts.caption:
Many orphaned giant anteater pups in Brazil are still nursing when their mothers are killed in road collisions. At rehabilitation centers, caregivers bottle-feed them, provide around-the-clock care, and help them build strength for a possible return to the wild. Nat Geo Explorer @fernando.faciole spent three years documenting these young animals and the people caring for them.

See how researchers are making Brazil's roads safer for giant anteaters at the link in bio.

posts.caption:
In the Alaska Peninsula, a brown bear surrounds a school of sockeye salmon that had journeyed thousands of miles upstream to the freshwaters of Alaska from the Pacific Ocean. Photographer @mikerigney told National Geographic this salmon migration was "easily one of the most beautiful natural displays I've ever seen."

See more Photos of the Day at the link in bio.

posts.caption:
Alzheimer’s disease symptoms and other forms of dementia don't occur overnight. Up to a decade before memory impairment appears, subtle cognitive symptoms can emerge. While these signs alone aren't definitive, recognizing patterns can help patients and families prepare for what lies ahead.

Learn more about these signs and what experts say patients and their families can do at the link in bio.

Photograph by Jason Edwards (@jasonedwardsng)

posts.caption:
Presented by @Rolex. Hunted for their scales and meat, pangolins are among the most heavily trafficked mammals in the world, with millions believed to have been harvested in Africa over recent decades. But in places like Cameroon, conservationists are working to protect these armored creatures. At the @tikkihywoodfoundation's rescue center, staff and minders tend to injured pangolins before rehabilitating them for release into the wild, managing complex care needs that can change from day to day. 

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in #AfricaEarthsWildHome. #PerpetualPlanet

Learn more about the efforts to save pangolins at the link in bio. 

Photographs by @marcuswestbergphotography

posts.caption: The shoebill’s prehistoric appearance makes it unique among living birds, with a look that matches fossils dating back millions of years. Its biology gets stranger still, with chicks attacking their own siblings and adults hunting everything from lungfish to baby crocodiles. Learn more about shoebills with these five facts.

posts.caption:
Presented by @Rolex. Madagascar is currently home to over one hundred species of lemurs that aren't found anywhere else on the planet, and scientists have uncovered evidence of even more lemur species that roamed Madagascar in the past, including giants that were far larger than any of today's lemurs.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

#AfricaEarthsWildHome is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

posts.caption:
Presented by @rolex. Around 40,000 tourists visit Bwindi Impenetrable National Park annually, bringing pathogens from around the world that can put the mountain gorillas who live there at risk. Veterinarian and Rolex National Geographic Perpetual Planet Explorer Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka is helping to protect these endangered primates through her pioneering One Health approach, which starts with treating the gorillas’ closest neighbors—focusing on diseases that can be transmitted between humans and animals.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in #AfricaEarthsWildHome. #PerpetualPlanet

Learn more about Kalema-Zikusoka pioneering work and this difficult-to-implement approach to wildlife conservation in the October issue of National Geographic and at the link in bio. 

Photograph by Robin Hammond (@hammond_robin)

posts.caption:
Photos by @joelsartore | Isn’t Dumpling just the cutest?

With short, stubby legs, it isn’t easy for striped skunks to outrun trouble, so they’ve developed a unique defense system to protect themselves from predators. When cornered, a skunk will first try to frighten the predator by turning its back, raising its tail, and arching its back while stomping its feet. If this display proves unsuccessful, the skunk will resort to spraying the animal with a strong-smelling fluid that can sting the eyes of the predator, giving the skunk just enough time to escape.

Photos taken @savannah_wrc_. To see more species featured in the Photo Ark, follow me @joelsartore. #PhotoArk

If this display proves unsuccessful, the skunk will resort to spraying the animal with a strong-smelling fluid that can sting the eyes of the predator, giving the skunk just enough time to escape.

Photos taken @savannah_wrc_. To see more species featured in the Photo Ark, follow me @joelsartore. #PhotoArk

posts.caption:
Women in this Sardinian mountain village have high odds of living to 100. Researchers have identified it as a new blue zone—a geographic region where residents aged 70 and older have exceptional rates of survival and longevity. Here, women who reach 70 are three times as likely to reach the century mark as their U.S. counterparts, so researchers are investigating whether factors such as diet, family life, and genetics could help explain that advantage.

Discover the clues to living a longer, healthier life at the link in bio.

Photograph by Marisa Montibeller

posts.caption:
A simple branch becomes a fishing rod in the hands of these resourceful chimpanzees. This technique allows them to harvest algae without getting wet.
 
Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet
 
Presented by @Rolex. #AfricaEarthsWildHome is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

posts.caption:
Presented by @Rolex. Conservation ecologist and Rolex National Geographic Perpetual Planet Explorer Matt Shirley has spent years working alongside scientists across Africa to uncover the secret lives of dwarf crocodiles, a timid species that emerges from burrows at night to feed. Despite thriving in a variety of ecosystems, the world’s smallest crocodiles are facing commercial overharvesting and habitat loss. Through his work, Shirley is discovering the ways these tenacious reptiles are hanging on and adapting to their ever-changing environment. 

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in #AfricaEarthsWildHome. #PerpetualPlanet

Discover more about dwarf crocodiles and the conservation plans to help them thrive at the link in bio.

Photograph by Robin Hammond (@hammond_robin)

posts.caption:
Presented by @Rolex. When the millionaire who owned the world's largest rhino herd ran out of money, the conservationists who took over responsibility for the herd in 2023 had an audacious idea: split 2,000 southern white rhinos into smaller groups and seed them across Africa. The goal is to protect them from poachers and ensure the species has the best chance of survival. While the plan is working, their mission is far from over. 

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in #AfricaEarthsWildHome. #PerpetualPlanet

Learn more about this historic plan to save the white rhino at the link in bio.

Photographs by @brentstirton

posts.caption:
Presented by @Rolex. It's time to explore nature on an epic scale. It's time to explore Africa. 

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

#AfricaEarthsWildHome is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

posts.caption:
Presented by @Rolex. When Matt Shirley first shone his flashlight into a cave in Gabon, dozens of crocodile eyes stared back at him. But these weren’t ordinary crocodiles. They were tiny, timid, and...orange. They had found an unlikely home underground, and an unusual source of food that helped them thrive. Discover more about the lives of Africa’s smallest crocodiles at the link in bio.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in #AfricaEarthsWildHome. #PerpetualPlanet

Photograph by @hammond_robin

Africa Earth’s Wild Home premieres Friday, October 2 at 8/7c on @NatGeoTV. Streaming next day on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

caption.text:
Presented by @Rolex. Welcome to Africa 🌍 Africa Earth’s Wild Home takes you deep into the heart of our wildest continent, bringing you closer to its animals, landscapes, and the people watching over it than ever before.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

Africa Earth’s Wild Home, narrated by @wunmimosaku, premieres Friday, October 2 at 8/7c on National Geographic. Streaming next day on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

caption.text:
Video and photos by @babaktafreshi | On Tuesday morning I photographed a celestial spectacle right in my backyard, near Boston. Hidden behind the moon for an hour, Jupiter reappeared from the dark night side of the moon, like a sparkling diamond. The rare phenomenon is called occultation. 

Slide 1: timelapse videos of the scene through a 600mm telephoto lens (cropped). Note the four lined up Galilean Moons of Jupiter. 
Slide 2: Moon is departing away from the alignment in twilight. 
Slide 3: An HDR image (3 exposures) to reveal the lunar details in both its bright dayside and the faint earthshine glow on the night side of the moon. 
Slide 4: A longer 30-second exposure on a star tracker has overexposed the moon to reveal the background starry sky.

We could stay here a while. 🌿

#Queens is streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

caption.text:
Presented by @Rolex. Fertile for just one week per year, this female fossa can't afford to be shy. 

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

#AfricaEarthsWildHome is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

caption.text:
Many orphaned giant anteater pups in Brazil are still nursing when their mothers are killed in road collisions. At rehabilitation centers, caregivers bottle-feed them, provide around-the-clock care, and help them build strength for a possible return to the wild. Nat Geo Explorer @fernando.faciole spent three years documenting these young animals and the people caring for them.

See how researchers are making Brazil's roads safer for giant anteaters at the link in bio.

caption.text:
In the Alaska Peninsula, a brown bear surrounds a school of sockeye salmon that had journeyed thousands of miles upstream to the freshwaters of Alaska from the Pacific Ocean. Photographer @mikerigney told National Geographic this salmon migration was "easily one of the most beautiful natural displays I've ever seen."

See more Photos of the Day at the link in bio.

Alzheimer’s disease symptoms and other forms of dementia don't occur overnight. Up to a decade before memory impairment appears, subtle cognitive symptoms can emerge. While these signs alone aren't definitive, recognizing patterns can help patients and families prepare for what lies ahead.

Learn more about these signs and what experts say patients and their families can do at the link in bio.

Photograph by Jason Edwards (@jasonedwardsng)

Presented by @Rolex. Hunted for their scales and meat, pangolins are among the most heavily trafficked mammals in the world, with millions believed to have been harvested in Africa over recent decades. But in places like Cameroon, conservationists are working to protect these armored creatures. At the @tikkihywoodfoundation's rescue center, staff and minders tend to injured pangolins before rehabilitating them for release into the wild, managing complex care needs that can change from day to day. 

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in #AfricaEarthsWildHome. #PerpetualPlanet

Learn more about the efforts to save pangolins at the link in bio. 

Photographs by @marcuswestbergphotography

caption.text: The shoebill’s prehistoric appearance makes it unique among living birds, with a look that matches fossils dating back millions of years. Its biology gets stranger still, with chicks attacking their own siblings and adults hunting everything from lungfish to baby crocodiles. Learn more about shoebills with these five facts.

caption.text:
Presented by @Rolex. Madagascar is currently home to over one hundred species of lemurs that aren't found anywhere else on the planet, and scientists have uncovered evidence of even more lemur species that roamed Madagascar in the past, including giants that were far larger than any of today's lemurs.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

#AfricaEarthsWildHome is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

caption.text:
Presented by @rolex. Around 40,000 tourists visit Bwindi Impenetrable National Park annually, bringing pathogens from around the world that can put the mountain gorillas who live there at risk. Veterinarian and Rolex National Geographic Perpetual Planet Explorer Gladys Kalema-Zikusoka is helping to protect these endangered primates through her pioneering One Health approach, which starts with treating the gorillas’ closest neighbors—focusing on diseases that can be transmitted between humans and animals.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in #AfricaEarthsWildHome. #PerpetualPlanet

Learn more about Kalema-Zikusoka pioneering work and this difficult-to-implement approach to wildlife conservation in the October issue of National Geographic and at the link in bio. 

Photograph by Robin Hammond (@hammond_robin)

Photos by @joelsartore | Isn’t Dumpling just the cutest?

With short, stubby legs, it isn’t easy for striped skunks to outrun trouble, so they’ve developed a unique defense system to protect themselves from predators. When cornered, a skunk will first try to frighten the predator by turning its back, raising its tail, and arching its back while stomping its feet. If this display proves unsuccessful, the skunk will resort to spraying the animal with a strong-smelling fluid that can sting the eyes of the predator, giving the skunk just enough time to escape.

Photos taken @savannah_wrc_. To see more species featured in the Photo Ark, follow me @joelsartore. #PhotoArk

This king penguin parent and its chick were among thousands that caught the eye of photographer Martin Gregus Jr. (@mywildlive) on South Georgia. King penguins have an unusually long reproductive cycle compared to other penguins, which means that eggs, chicks, and adults can all be present within a colony at the same time.

Presented by @Rolex. Meet the dwarf crocodiles thriving in the darkness of Gabon’s caves. From hunting bats to navigating cave floors coated in guano, these remarkable reptiles have found unexpected ways to survive. Learn more about Africa's tiny crocs and Matt Shirley's research at the link in bio.

Photographs by @hammond_robin
 
#AfricaEarthsWildHome is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

Women in this Sardinian mountain village have high odds of living to 100. Researchers have identified it as a new blue zone—a geographic region where residents aged 70 and older have exceptional rates of survival and longevity. Here, women who reach 70 are three times as likely to reach the century mark as their U.S. counterparts, so researchers are investigating whether factors such as diet, family life, and genetics could help explain that advantage.

Discover the clues to living a longer, healthier life at the link in bio.

Photograph by Marisa Montibeller

Presented by @Rolex. Would you ever have guessed that flamingos are growing their own food with the help of fiddler crabs? This arrangement is so unusual, it's never been seen anywhere else on Earth.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

See more extraordinary animal behavior in #AfricaEarthsWildHome, now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

caption.text:
A simple branch becomes a fishing rod in the hands of these resourceful chimpanzees. This technique allows them to harvest algae without getting wet.
 
Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet
 
Presented by @Rolex. #AfricaEarthsWildHome is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

Presented by @Rolex. Conservation ecologist and Rolex National Geographic Perpetual Planet Explorer Matt Shirley has spent years working alongside scientists across Africa to uncover the secret lives of dwarf crocodiles, a timid species that emerges from burrows at night to feed. Despite thriving in a variety of ecosystems, the world’s smallest crocodiles are facing commercial overharvesting and habitat loss. Through his work, Shirley is discovering the ways these tenacious reptiles are hanging on and adapting to their ever-changing environment. 

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in #AfricaEarthsWildHome. #PerpetualPlanet

Discover more about dwarf crocodiles and the conservation plans to help them thrive at the link in bio.

Photograph by Robin Hammond (@hammond_robin)

Presented by @Rolex. When the millionaire who owned the world's largest rhino herd ran out of money, the conservationists who took over responsibility for the herd in 2023 had an audacious idea: split 2,000 southern white rhinos into smaller groups and seed them across Africa. The goal is to protect them from poachers and ensure the species has the best chance of survival. While the plan is working, their mission is far from over. 

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in #AfricaEarthsWildHome. #PerpetualPlanet

Learn more about this historic plan to save the white rhino at the link in bio.

Photographs by @brentstirton

Presented by @Rolex. He’s spent six months underground, and now he’s looking for love—but when a female answers his call, this black frog seems to have second thoughts.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

#AfricaEarthsWildHome is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

caption.text:
Presented by @Rolex. When Matt Shirley first shone his flashlight into a cave in Gabon, dozens of crocodile eyes stared back at him. But these weren’t ordinary crocodiles. They were tiny, timid, and...orange. They had found an unlikely home underground, and an unusual source of food that helped them thrive. Discover more about the lives of Africa’s smallest crocodiles at the link in bio.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in #AfricaEarthsWildHome. #PerpetualPlanet

Photograph by @hammond_robin

Africa Earth’s Wild Home premieres Friday, October 2 at 8/7c on @NatGeoTV. Streaming next day on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

Presented by @Rolex. Welcome to Africa 🌍 Africa Earth’s Wild Home takes you deep into the heart of our wildest continent, bringing you closer to its animals, landscapes, and the people watching over it than ever before.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

Africa Earth’s Wild Home, narrated by @wunmimosaku, premieres Friday, October 2 at 8/7c on National Geographic. Streaming next day on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.
